nodes.name: Cartographic Division
nodes.excerpt: The Cartographic Division manages navigational charts and coastal data.
nodes.notes:
- The Cartographic Division is part of the Admiralty.
- It maintains official navigational charts, survey records, and coastal data.
- Located in Tiveck, it occupies the upper two floors of the Admiralty's main building.
- Its archive is in a separate, humidity-controlled vault in the basement.
- The Division employs about 45 people.
- Staff includes 14 active surveyors, 12 chart drafters, 8 archivists, and 11 administrative staff.
- Chief Surveyor Vane nominally heads the Division.
- Vane is elderly and delegates operational responsibility to deputy Harwick Ossel.
- Vane works three mornings a week, leaving before midday.
- The Division's records are authoritative for coastal rights, territorial claims, and navigational precedent.
- Access to the archive is a form of institutional power.
- Admiralty personnel can access the archive by request.
- Guild representatives have access under a formal agreement.
- Third parties need explicit authorization from the Chief Surveyor or deputy.
- Unauthorized access to the archive is a criminal matter.
- Two incidents in the past decade involved discrepancies in survey data.
- Discrepancies were due to instrument calibration errors.
- Affected routes were deprioritized for Admiralty patrol.
- The Division's relationship with the Deepwater Guild is formally cooperative.
- The Guild has challenged the Division's data when it affects operational reach.
- Disputes with the Guild are usually resolved quietly.

nodes.name: Rella Corse
nodes.excerpt: Rella Corse filed a complaint against Harwick Ossel.
nodes.notes:
- Rella Corse filed a complaint alleging that Harwick Ossel supplied altered survey data to a private concern.
- The complaint suggested the data was used to keep Admiralty patrol routes predictable and away from certain anchorages.
- Corse was dismissed eight months before Ossel's promotion.

- Rella Corse served as a Navigator First Class in the Admiralty for eleven years before her dismissal.
- The official reason for Rella Corse's dismissal was 'conduct inconsistent with the duties of the navigational corps.'
- Rella Corse filed a formal complaint against a senior officer, Harwick Ossel, alleging he falsified survey coordinates.
- The complaint against Harwick Ossel was investigated and closed without findings, and Ossel was promoted.
- After her dismissal, Rella Corse worked for two years doing freelance chart correction for independent merchants in the harbor district.
- Rella Corse lived in a rented room above a fish saltery in Salt Warren during her freelance work period.
- Rella Corse met Dovan Strake during her time in Salt Warren, though the nature of their introduction is unknown.
- Rella Corse is in her early forties and is described as lean with deliberate movements.
- Rella Corse keeps her hair cut short.
- Rella Corse carries a brass sighting instrument as a habit.
- Rella Corse currently resides in a rented storehouse at the edge of the 14th Lowland, living alone.
- Rella Corse is formal with new acquaintances and relaxed with almost no one, except possibly Dovan Strake.
- Rella Corse and Dovan Strake have a long-running argument that is not clearly antagonistic or friendly.
- Rella Corse has not filed any documents with the Admiralty since her dismissal.
- Rella Corse does not speak about Harwick Ossel.
- Rella Corse has been seen near the archive corridor at the Deepwater Guild's lower hall but is not known to have entered.

- Rella Corse has stated that her arrangement with the Inkhand is functional and that she does not ask unnecessary questions.

- Rella Corse is one of the founding members of the Tide Compact, formed twelve years ago.
- She runs the logistics side of the Tide Compact from a leased storehouse at the edge of the 14th Lowland.
- Uses the warehouse's legitimate salt-drying contracts as cover for the Compact's operations.
- Has a reputation for cutting loose anyone who draws attention to the operation.
- At least three former associates of the Compact have disappeared from the harbor district without explanation.

Those who served with her suggest the real issue was a formal complaint she filed against a senior officer named Harwick Ossel, who she claimed had been falsifying survey coordinates to steer Admiralty vessels away from routes controlled by his private interests. nodes.name: Shōyō Hinata
nodes.excerpt: Shōyō Hinata is the main protagonist of the Haikyū!! series.
nodes.notes:
Shōyō Hinata is the main protagonist of the Haikyū!! series by Haruichi Furudate.
Hinata was a first-year student at Karasuno High and a middle blocker for the Boys' Volleyball Team.
In 2018, he joined MSBY Black Jackals, a Division 1 team in the V-League.
He became a member of Japan Men's National Volleyball Team during the 2021 Olympics.
As of 2022, Hinata is a member of Asas São Paulo in the Brazil Super League.
Hinata is the older brother of Natsu Hinata.
Upon entering high school, Hinata was 162.8 cm tall and grew to 164.2 cm.
He is the second shortest person on the Karasuno volleyball team.
Hinata has unruly orange hair and brown eyes.
He typically wears his Karasuno school uniform and a black volleyball jersey with number 10.
Post-timeskip, Hinata grew his hair out and trained in Brazil, reaching a height of 172 cm.
Hinata has a cheerful and energetic personality, easily excited and loud.
He is simpleminded but observant, empathetic, and a natural schmoozer.
Hinata has a serious attitude towards volleyball and plays with great tenacity.
He gets scared easily but recovers quickly to challenge opponents.
Initially, Hinata was nervous before matches but improved over time.
Hinata struggles academically but improves with motivation and guidance.
Hinata was inspired by the Small Giant from Karasuno High's volleyball match.
He joined Yukigaoka Junior High's volleyball club as the only member initially.
Hinata's team lost to Kitagawa Daiichi Junior High, but he impressed Kageyama.
Hinata vowed to defeat Kageyama and trained rigorously to improve.
He travels to Karasuno each morning by a thirty-minute bike ride.
Hinata entered Karasuno High determined to get revenge on Kageyama.

nodes.filePreview: **Shōyō Hinata** is the main protagonist of the Haikyū!! series by Haruichi Furudate. Hinata was a first-year student at Karasuno High and a middle blocker for the Boys' Volleyball Team. In 2018, he joined MSBY Black Jackals, a Division 1 team in the V-League. He became a member of Japan Men's National Volleyball Team during the 2021 Olympics. As of 2022, Hinata is a member of Asas São Paulo in the Brazil Super League. nodes.name: The Inkhand
nodes.excerpt: The Inkhand is a mysterious broker of the Tide Compact.
nodes.notes:
- The Inkhand is the third founding member of the Tide Compact.
- The Inkhand's identity is unknown.
- The Inkhand communicates through written notes in reddish ink.
- The Inkhand's notes are unsigned except for a hand mark in the same ink.
- The handwriting is precise and unhurried, suggesting formal scribal training.
- The Inkhand has access to Admiralty survey data and Deepwater Guild records.
- Speculation exists that the Inkhand is an archivist or scribe.
- Rella Corse describes the Inkhand arrangement as functional.
- Dovan Strake avoids discussing the Inkhand.
- Maren Ashveil is mentioned in connection with the Inkhand by an unreliable source.
- The Inkhand has not been identified by anyone who confirmed the identification.
- The Inkhand might be more than one person or a fictional entity.
- The Inkhand might be someone known in the harbor district without recognition.

- The Inkhand is a founding member of the Tide Compact.

- Speculated to be a scribe or archivist with access to restricted records.

nodes.filePreview:
The Inkhand is a name that appears in accounts of the Tide Compact as its third founding member, a broker or intermediary whose actual identity has never been established. What is known — or at least consistently reported — is as follows.

The Inkhand communicates exclusively through written notes, using a distinctive reddish ink that some sources describe as rust-colored and others as dried-blood dark. The notes are always unsigned except for a small pressed mark: a hand, palm-forward, rendered in the same ink. Recipients describe the handwriting as precise and unhurried, the kind produced…

nodes.name: The Tide Compact
nodes.excerpt: The Tide Compact is a smuggling consortium formed to profit from contraband.
nodes.notes:
- The Tide Compact was formed twelve years ago on the salt flats north of Tiveck.
- Three rival smuggling consortiums formed The Tide Compact.
- Founding members: Rella Corse, Dovan Strake, and the Inkhand.
- Rella Corse is a former Navigator of the Admiralty, dismissed for sealed reasons.
- Dovan Strake is a fence operating out of a chandlery in Salt Warren.
- The Inkhand's identity is unconfirmed.
- The Compact's business involves contraband goods classified by the Admiralty.
- Goods include preserved meats, salvaged navigational instruments, and contested documents.
- Rella Corse manages logistics from a storehouse at the edge of the 14th Lowland.
- Rella Corse uses salt-drying contracts as cover for operations.
- Rella Corse is meticulous, rarely speaks above a murmur, and cuts loose those who draw attention.
- At least three former associates disappeared from the harbor district.
- Dovan Strake handles buyers and launders proceeds of document theft.
- Dovan Strake is affable, loud, and well-liked, drinks at the Wrecked Compass.
- The Inkhand's role is unclear, possibly connected to the Deepwater Guild.
- The Compact does not compete directly with the Deepwater Guild.
- Debate exists on whether the Compact has an arrangement with the Deepwater Guild or is too small to crush.
nodes.filePreview:
The Tide Compact was formed twelve years ago on the salt flats north of Tiveck, when three rival smuggling consortiums agreed to stop killing each other long enough to turn a profit. Its founding members were Rella Corse, a former Navigator of the Admiralty who had been quietly dismissed for reasons that remain sealed; Dovan Strake, a fence operating out of a chandlery in Salt Warren; and an unnamed broker known only as the Inkhand, whose identity has never been confirmed.
